modalities.value: web browsing; text, images, and PDFs; user files; Python code execution

source.quote:
Deep research leverages reasoning to search, interpret, and analyze
massive amounts of text, images, and PDFs on the internet, pivoting as needed in reaction to
information it encounters. It can also read files provided by the user and analyze data by writing
and executing python code.

reasoningModes.value: reasoning / chain-of-thought; ChatGPT uses a custom-prompted o3-mini to summarize chains of thought

source.quote:
Deep research leverages reasoning to search, interpret, and analyze
massive amounts of text, images, and PDFs on the internet

architecture.value: early version of OpenAI o3 optimized for web browsing

source.quote:
The deep research model is powered by an early version of OpenAI o3 that is
optimized for web browsing.

trainingData.value: new browsing datasets for research use cases; o1 safety datasets; new browsing-specific safety datasets

source.quote: Deep research was trained on new browsing datasets created specifically for research use cases.

topics.headline: Standard and challenging disallowed-content not_unsafe / not_overrefuse evaluations

source.quote:
We evaluated deep research against GPT-4o, OpenAI o1-mini, and o1 to ensure
the model does not comply with requests for disallowed content.

topics.headline: Post-launch monitoring includes child safety risks

source.quote:
After launches, we actively monitor for misuse, including risks
related to child safety, cybersecurity threats, and violence.

topics.headline: Challenge red-teaming spans self-harm among other categories

source.quote:
We re-ran deep research against a dataset
containing the hardest examples discovered during OpenAI o3-mini red teaming, spanning
categories such as criminal behavior, self-harm, and hateful content.

topics.headline: [StrongReject](/evals/strongreject) jailbreak accuracy 0.93 for deep research (higher is better)

source.quote:
Jailbreak Evaluation: We evaluated deep-research on StrongReject[1], an academic jailbreak
benchmark that tests a model’s resistance against common attacks from the literature.

topics.headline: New prompt-injection eval; post-mitigation attack success mostly 0%

source.quote: For deep research, unmitigated prompt injections may result in two categories of harm:

topics.headline: Agentic tasks for resource acquisition / autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA); dual-use cyber CTFs

source.quote:
Autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA) is the process by which models acquire intelligence
by acquiring more resources in the real world, and is a key axis of our model autonomy threat
model.

topics.headline: PersonQA accuracy 0.86 (higher is better) and hallucination rate 0.13 (lower is better)

source.quote:
To evaluate hallucinations, we use the PersonQA dataset which contains 18 categories
of facts about people.

MakeMeSay is an automated contextual evaluation designed to measure models’ deception
capabilities, in the context of a model’s ability to get the other party (an AI model simulating a
human) to say a codeword.

The deep research model underwent the BBQ evaluation[2], a specialized test
designed to identify the tendency of the model to stereotype.

MakeMePay is an automated, open-sourced contextual evaluation designed to measure models’
manipulative capabilities, in the context of one model persuading the other to make a payment.

topics.headline: CTF Medium risk; first model rated medium in cybersecurity

source.quote:
Deep research sufficiently advances real-world vulnerability exploitation capabilities
to indicate Medium risk.

topics.headline: CBRN Medium; long-form refuse post-mitigation; wet-lab and [WMDP](/evals/wmdp) scores

source.quote:
Our evaluations found that deep research can help experts with the operational
planning of reproducing a known biological threat, which meets our medium risk threshold.

testers.name: Lysios LLC
testers.scope: External red teaming organization for deep research risks

testers.name: Signature Science
testers.scope: Biosecurity novelty probing of Pre-Mitigation deep research for novel biological threat ideation

source.quote:
Biosecurity experts from Signature Science probed the Pre-Mitigation deep research model for
conceptual ideation of designing novel biological threats.

testers.name: Gryphon Scientific
testers.scope: Designed long-form biorisk questions and rubrics; co-created tacit knowledge troubleshooting set

source.quote:
We designed the questions and detailed rubrics with Gryphon Scientific due to their expertise
working with dangerous biological agents in a national security setting.

findings.text: Safety Advisory Group classified deep research as overall medium risk across cybersecurity, persuasion, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN), and model autonomy — the first OpenAI model rated medium for cybersecurity.

source.quote:
Safety Advisory Group [3] classified the deep research model as overall medium risk, including
medium risk for cybersecurity, persuasion, CBRN, model autonomy. This is the first time a model
is rated medium risk in cybersecurity.

findings.text: After removing browsing-contaminated [Capture the Flag (CTF)](/evals/openai-ctf-suite) trajectories, post-mitigation deep research with and without browsing performed within each other's margin of error, so CTF uplift from browsing was mainly contamination.

source.quote:
After filtering out attempts where the model successfully found hints
or solutions online, the success rates for post-mitigation deep research models—with and without
browsing—fall within the margin of error of each other.

findings.text: Biology evaluations indicate models are on the cusp of meaningfully helping novices create known biological threats (the High threshold), though post-mitigation models scored 0% on long-form physical success steps.

source.quote:
Several of our biology evaluations indicate our models are on the cusp of being able to meaningfully
help novices create known biological threats, which would cross our high risk threshold.

findings.text: ChangeMyView persuasiveness for deep research and peers is roughly the 80–90th human percentile (range only; no single point score).

source.quote:
All models including deep research demonstrate strong performance on our ChangeMyView
evaluation, scoring within the top 80–90th percentile of humans

findings.text: PersonQA hallucination rate may overstate deep research errors because some model outputs were accurate while the test set was out of date.

source.quote:
Upon further examination, we found that the hallucination rate noted above actually overstates
how often deep research hallucinates, because in some instances its outputs were accurate and
the information in our test set was out of date.

findings.text: Residual prompt-injection risk remains because real-world attacks may exceed the evaluation set.

source.quote:
We anticipate that some real-world prompt injection
attacks will be more advanced than our evaluation set. Consequently, there is still some residual
risk that prompt injections encountered when deployed can impact model behavior.

findings.text: Many preparedness capability numbers appear only in charts: [BioLP-Bench](/evals/biolp-bench) absolute scores, contextual nuclear multiple-choice question (MCQ) absolutes, OpenAI pull requests (PRs) absolute rates, agentic tasks, and SWE-Lancer dollars chart detail beyond the stated 53%/$87,708.

source.quote:
Pre-Mitigation deep research without browsing and Post-Mitigation deep research with browsing
score highest on this eval.

findings.text: SWE-Lancer results note a July 17, 2025 update; the card says all dollars-earned figures below were updated accordingly.

source.quote:
On July 17th, 2025, we released an updated version of SWE-Lancer,
accessible on GitHub.
